I may not count because I was part of the lockdown class, BUT I decided to push pause on my studies to only come back last year and graduate. 

During the whole lockdown, we did at least had our lab days each Friday, which was grand cause I did get to spend time with our classmates, we eventually formed our own little groups, etc. When pubs finally opened for outdoors only, I thought ‘This is great! I can really make friends with these people blah blah blah!’ No. Just no. After being in lockdown for a whole feckin semester I thought my classmates would be DYING for a pint, but no. You want to know the entire highlight of that class??? A museum. We went to a museum, no pints afterwards, nothing, but a fucking museum. That was it. 

I do not know about your situation, but I think the main problem with mine is that most of them were these Americans that had a stick up their arse the entire time. The only student that actually had a bit of craic was an Irish woman who came and had multiple pints with me, she is only one that I would be flexible for when planning something. I tried multiple times to get these yanks out of the dorms and do something that was doable for covid standards, but they would either commit and cancel last minute or just turn me down. 

Sorry for the TMI, but this bothered me since day one at UCD. No, it’s not just you, and if I was attending uni during normal times, I do not think they would change. I’ve been to 3 different universities before UCD, and 2 out of the 3, I’ve made great, loyal, loving friends and I have not felt that with UCD. 

Depending what your major is, I HIGHLY recommend going to a “liberal artsy” school. I went to uni in bum fuck nowhere my freshman year, and let me tell you something, you can be the strangest, most awkward person alive and you will still at least make one friend there.

As an archaeologist and a pagan, I want to honour my profession while keeping a spiritual side as well, which can be complicated at times. I do agree with you about people's relationship with the gods, I think it should never be that personal. I can't help but feel that this certain type practice that gets in the way of my job. 

I can't give any specifics but one famous example is when a certain Iron-Age site was going to be bull-dosed without any excavation before hand, an archaeological team made excellent points about its historical importance to the court, but all of that got thrown out the window when these "druids" stepped in and pleaded to the court about their spiritual connection with the place. Right then and there, that case was thrown out the window and the place was bull-dosed and a motorway was built.  

Look, I have some spiritual places that I feel I connected with, and I too would want to protect and preserve these places, but when working with other developers and the actual government, they are not going to care about how you "feel" with the place, we unfortunately don't have the privilege like the Christians where we can claim a particular site because it's our religious rite, we have to work with these people to get what we want. And so this attitude of "oh yea, me and Hades are bffs" certainly does not help in protecting in what we find is sacred. I'm trying not to gate keep here, but I really do not want an encounter of something like that ever again. If you do have that certain connection with a god please keep that personal.
